chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'A man gave his wife the choice [of divorce].' He said, 'The choice is hers as long as they remain in their session; when they separate, she no longer has the choice.'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The right of option or choice.
key_terms.تَخْيِير: The act of giving a choice, specifically referring to a husband offering his wife the option of divorce.
key_terms.مَجْلِس: A session or gathering; in this context, the specific time and place where the divorce option is exercised.

ai.seo_question: When does a wife's right to choose divorce (takhyyir) expire after her husband offers it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundary of *takhyyir*, a specific form of divorce where the husband grants his wife the agency to choose between remaining married or accepting separation. The ruling emphasizes that this option is strictly bound to the immediate context of the proposal; once the parties disperse from that session, the right lapses, preventing indefinite uncertainty in marital status. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of minimizing ambiguity (*gharar*) in legal transactions by anchoring rights to specific, observable circumstances.
